S3.dek: The university's release lists what prepared the data. An automated 2D/3D pavement laser scanner, and "a TxDOT-donated mobile research van".

The equipment Ingram School of Engineering

S4.hook: Depth tells a crack from a stain.
S4.dek: The system pairs 2D photos with 3D depth maps. It ranks severe hazards like crumbling concrete above minor surface cracks.
labels: The surface 2D photo and 3D depth map

S5.hook: The old rating read a sample.
S5.dek: Manual collection happened at "a sampled portion of the pavement section". The university describes the new reading as "pixel-level detection of pavement damage".
labels: The extent In plan, one lane

S6.dek: Wang describes the purpose as reducing reliance on traditional human inspection. The four words below are his.

S7.hook: An engineer still has to check.
S7.dek: The team's own 2025 paper says the precision of the technology often leads to inaccuracies.
labels: Those inaccuracies "must be verified by pavement engineers."

S8.hook: Thin cracks still score the lowest.
S8.dek: The largest gain came on the thinnest cracks.
labels: The measurement Two published F1 scores
